mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in at least 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous year - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered months, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and prompts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the trigger is not followed by a decline in earnings reports.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 6% combined with a federal funds rate below 2% signals high inflation with loose monetary policy, creating uncertainty and volatility that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate policy shifts.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered months, or the trigger is followed by a policy tightening that produces negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered months, or the trigger is followed by negative earnings surprises.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a synchronized weakening in demand components, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in late-cycle conditions.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous month - 1% AND HOUST < previous month - 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 does not exhibit statistically significant negative returns in at least 50% of triggered late-cycle periods, or the trigger is not followed by a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate by more than 0.75 percentage points within a single month signals an emergency monetary easing in response to financial stress, which stabilizes markets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered emergency easing episodes, or the trigger is followed by continued market decline.
